periods.title: Economical and Social Progress in Uttar Pradesh
periods.tagline: The Progress of Uttar Pradesh Is the Progress of New India — Balanced Economic Growth and Social Justice Are the True Pillars of a Developed U.P.
periods.overview: This page and the following 21st Century page both describe contemporary Uttar Pradesh, but with a deliberately different emphasis: where the 21st Century page traces headline growth and infrastructure achievements, this page focuses specifically on the persistent gap between U.P.'s economic scale — the second-largest state economy in India, the largest workforce of any state — and its human development indicators, which continue to trail the national average on literacy, female literacy, institutional childbirth, and child health by real, NFHS-5-documented margins. That gap is not a new phenomenon this page discovers in isolation; it is the latest chapter in a pattern visible across this entire track, from the Later Mughals' Awadh-centred prosperity coexisting with rural revenue extraction, through the British colonial economy's simultaneous infrastructure investment and deindustrialisation, to independent India's own uneven regional development between the historically prosperous Doab and the persistently lagging Purvanchal and Bundelkhand regions the Reorganisation page discusses. Read as the continuation of that long pattern rather than a standalone snapshot, this page's core policy question — how to convert U.P.'s genuine scale advantages into more evenly distributed social outcomes — is really the latest version of a challenge this region's administrators have been managing, with varying success, for centuries.

phases.name: Economic Overview
points: GSDP (Nominal): approx. ₹24.89 lakh crore, 2nd in India; share in India's GSDP: approx. 8.3%; per capita income (2022–23): approx. ₹57,033, below the national average
Workforce (2023): 10.2 crore+, the highest of any state; contribution to FDI inflow (2000–2023): approx. 5%, among the top 5 states; Ease of Doing Business Rank 2020: 2nd

phases.name: Agricultural & Industrial Base
points: Largest producer of foodgrains in India; highest sugarcane production; leading state in milk production; success of the 'Mukhya Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana', crop diversification, soil health mission

U.P. is an emerging industrial hub of North India — textiles, leather, handicrafts, brassware, glassware, sports goods, food processing, IT/ITeS; Noida, Greater Noida, Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA) are major industrial growth engines; One District One Product (ODOP) initiative promotes local products globally

phases.name: Investment & Infrastructure
points: 'UP Investors Summit' has attracted large investments and MoUs; industrial corridors — DMIC influence, Bundelkhand Industrial Development Authority; Film City (Noida), Toy City (Greater Noida), Electronics Manufacturing Policy

Infrastructure: Purvanchal Expressway, Bundelkhand Expressway, Ganga Expressway, four-laning of rural roads; Dedicated Freight Corridor, Vande Bharat trains, station modernisation; Jewar Airport (Noida), Kushinagar, Ayodhya, Gorakhpur, Chitrakoot Airports; Smart Cities — Lucknow, Kanpur, Varanasi, Agra, Prayagraj

phases.name: Social Development
points: Literacy rate (15+ years): 67.7% in U.P. vs 77.7% nationally; female literacy rate: 59.4% vs 70.3% nationally; school enrolment (6–14 years): 97.1% vs 96.5% nationally

Institutional delivery: 79.8% vs 88.6% nationally; Infant Mortality Rate: 37 per 1000 live births vs 28 nationally; Maternal Mortality Ratio: 155 per lakh live births vs 97 nationally; stunting in children under 5: 43.1% vs 35.5% nationally

Education and Human Development.intro: The specific schemes named here (Kanya Vidya Dhan, Mission Shakti, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao) are worth distinguishing from the similarly named national schemes discussed on the national India 2011–2020 and India 2020–Present pages — several are U.P.-specific implementations or variants rather than identical national programmes.
points: Expansion of basic education infrastructure — schools, colleges, universities; launch of Kanya Vidya Dhan, Mission Shakti, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao; new universities — BBAU, Central University of South Asia, Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (Central University); skill development through the Kaushal Vikas Mission; improvement in digital education and e-governance in schools

Health and Nutrition.intro: Reading this category's list of expanding facilities (PHCs, CHCs, medical colleges) against the overview's NFHS-5 statistics above makes clear that infrastructure expansion and actual outcome improvement are two distinct things worth tracking separately — the state has been building capacity faster than health indicators have caught up to the national average.
points: Expansion of healthcare facilities — PHCs, CHCs, district hospitals, medical colleges; Ayushman Bharat covers a large number of beneficiaries; Mission Indradhanush, Nikshay Mitra, TB control programmes; nutritional support through ICDS, POSHAN Abhiyaan, mid-day meal scheme

Social Welfare and Inclusion.intro: This category's list of welfare schemes overlaps substantially with national programmes (PM Awas Yojana, NFSA) — the specific U.P. contribution worth noting here is less the scheme names themselves than the sheer scale at which they must operate, given the state's status as India's most populous.
points: Reservation policies for SCs, STs, OBCs and EWS; welfare schemes — Old Age Pension, Widow Pension, Divyang Pension; Housing for All, Ujjwala Yojana, PM Awas Yojana; free ration under NFSA, health insurance; upliftment of weaker sections and empowerment of women through self-help groups; promotion of minority welfare and inclusive development

Poverty Alleviation, Employment & Women'.intro: The women's empowerment statistics here (33% Panchayati Raj reservation, growing SHG participation) are a useful point of comparison against the more historically distant women's status discussions on much earlier pages in this track, like the Vedic Age and Gupta Period pages — a way of tracking how the same basic question has evolved across the entire chronology.
points: Decline in the poverty ratio over the decades; MGNREGA — rural employment and asset creation; self-employment schemes — PMEGP, ODOP, MUDRA loans; growth in the service sector and urban employment

Mission Shakti — women's safety, security and empowerment; increase in women's SHGs and financial inclusion; 33% reservation in Panchayati Raj Institutions; Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana, Matru Vandana Yojana; more women's participation in education, workforce and entrepreneurship

Culture, Tourism, Heritage & Challenges.intro: The heritage sites listed here — Varanasi, Ayodhya, Mathura, Sarnath, Kushinagar — are, without exception, places this track has already covered in historical depth on much earlier pages; this category shows how directly ancient religious geography continues to drive present-day economic activity through tourism.
points: Rich cultural heritage — Varanasi, Ayodhya, Mathura, Sarnath, Kushinagar, Prayagraj, Dudhwa; promotion of spiritual, eco and heritage tourism; Kumbh Mela, Dev Deepawali, Ramayana Circuit boosting the economy; conservation of monuments and promotion of local arts and handicrafts

Challenges: regional imbalance — Purvanchal and Bundelkhand lag behind; low per capita income and industrialisation in some regions; unemployment and underemployment; low literacy and health indicators compared to the national average; population pressure, urban congestion, pollution and environmental degradation

Agrarian Base, Industrial Clusters & ODO: Agricultural Powerhouse: India's leading producer of food grains, sugarcane, wheat, potatoes, and milk; irrigated by extensive canal networks (Sharda Canal, Upper Ganga Canal, Lower Ganga Canal) and groundwater tube-wells; Western UP characterized by high productivity cash-crop farming.

Specialized Industrial Clusters: 1. Leather & Footwear: Kanpur and Agra, 2. Textile & Handloom: Varanasi (Banarasi Silk), Mau, Kanpur ("Manchester of the East"), 3. Brassware & Metal: Moradabad ("Peetal Nagari"), 4. Glassware: Firozabad ("Suhag Nagari"), 5. Locks & Hardware: Aligarh, 6. Wooden Carvings: Saharanpur, 7. Handmade Carpets: Bhadohi and Mirzapur, 8. Chikan Embroidery & Zardozi: Lucknow, 9. Perfume (Ittar): Kannauj ("Perfume Capital of India").

One District One Product (ODOP): Pioneering state flagship scheme launched in January 2018; promotes, finances, brands, and exports distinct indigenous artisanal crafts and agro-products across all 75 districts; adopted as a national model by the Government of India.

women.name: Women's economic participation
women.note: Growth in women's SHGs, financial inclusion, and entrepreneurship under Mission Shakti and related schemes.

events.title: U.P.'s GSDP reaches ₹24.89 lakh crore
events.desc: Uttar Pradesh consolidates its position as India's 2nd largest state economy by nominal GSDP.

events.title: NFHS-5 data released
events.desc: The National Family Health Survey highlights continued gaps between U.P. and national averages on literacy, institutional delivery, and child health indicators.

prelims: The One District One Product (ODOP) scheme was first conceptualized and launched by the Government of Uttar Pradesh in January 2018.
Uttar Pradesh ranks first in India in the production of wheat, sugarcane, potatoes, and milk.
Kanpur was historically acclaimed as the "Manchester of the East" due to its flourishing textile mills and leather tanneries.
Kannauj in Uttar Pradesh is celebrated as the "Perfume Capital of India" (Ittar Nagari) for its traditional hydro-distilled floral fragrances.
Bhadohi district in Uttar Pradesh is globally renowned as the "Carpet City" of South Asia, holding a registered GI tag for handmade carpets.
Moradabad is internationally famous as the "Brass City" (Peetal Nagari) for its brass handicraft exports.
The Sharda Canal, commissioned in 1928, is the longest canal network in Uttar Pradesh, irrigating the Rohilkhand and Awadh plains.
mains: Evaluate the achievements, institutional design, and export impact of the One District One Product (ODOP) initiative in reviving traditional handicrafts in Uttar Pradesh.
Analyze the regional economic disparities between Western Uttar Pradesh, Purvanchal, and Bundelkhand, recommending policy interventions for balanced regional development.
Discuss the challenges facing agriculture in Uttar Pradesh with specific reference to land fragmentation, sugarcane pricing, and groundwater depletion.

periods.title: Uttar Pradesh in 21st Century
periods.tagline: Viksit Uttar Pradesh Is the Foundation of Viksit Bharat
periods.overview: This page closes out the Uttar Pradesh track by describing the region in its most current form — the same Ganga-Yamuna Doab that hosted the Vedic Janapadas, the Mauryan and Gupta provincial core, and the Mughal imperial capital now pursuing expressways, semiconductor and electronics manufacturing, international airports, and an explicit long-term vision of 'Viksit Uttar Pradesh' timed to India's own 2047 centenary goals. What makes this page worth reading as a genuine conclusion to the whole track, rather than simply the most recent data point, is how visibly its priorities echo the region's much older history: the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor and Ayodhya Dham developments described here are modern infrastructure investments in exactly the same religious geography — Varanasi and Ayodhya — that the Vedic Age, Mahajanapadas, and Gupta Period pages earlier in this track already identified as the region's oldest and most consistently significant sacred cities. Equally, this page's stated challenges — regional disparity between Purvanchal/Bundelkhand and the rest of the state, urban congestion, and the need for balanced development — are recognisably the same structural tensions between concentrated prosperity and uneven regional development that this track has traced, in one form or another, from the Delhi Sultanate's Doab-centred administration through the colonial-era United Provinces and into the present day.

phases.name: Economic Growth & Development
points: GSDP (current prices): ₹20.51 lakh crore, 2nd in India; share in India's GSDP: approx. 8.6%; per capita income: approx. ₹46,817, below the national average

NSDP growth rate (2023–24): 12.8%, 1st among large states; FDI inflow (Apr 2000–Dec 2023): US$20+ Billion, a top state; Ease of Doing Business Rank 2020: 2nd; strong growth in services, manufacturing, IT/ITeS and exports

phases.name: Industry, Investment & Infrastructure
points: Industrial corridors — DMIC, Bundelkhand, Purvanchal Expressway, Ganga Expressway; major sectors — electronics, food processing, textile, leather, furniture, defence, handicrafts

'One District One Product' (ODOP) is a flagship programme; thriving start-up ecosystem (Lucknow, Noida, Kanpur, Varanasi hubs); regular Investors Summits — U.P. Global Investors Summit; expressways, dedicated freight corridors, Vande Bharat trains, international airports (Noida/Jewar, Kushinagar); power-surplus state with a focus on solar and renewable energy

phases.name: Governance, Social Justice & Culture
points: Focus on transparent, accountable, technology-driven governance — e-District, online services, DigiLocker, Jan Suvidha Kendras; Swachh Bharat Mission, Mission Shakti (women's safety & empowerment); law & order modernisation — 112, CCTNS, e-FIR

Social justice & welfare schemes — PM Awas Yojana, Ujjwala Yojana, PM Kisan Samman Nidhi, Ayushman Bharat, Mission Shakti, Kanya Sumangala Yojana, Antyodaya Anna Yojana; culture & heritage — development of the Ramayana, Buddhist and Krishna spiritual circuits, Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, Ayodhya Dham, Mathura-Vrindavan Corridor, Prayagraj Mahakumbh (2019, 2025)

Social Development and Human Capital.intro: This category's specific schemes (Samagra Shiksha, Kaushal Vikas Mission) should be read as this decade's version of the same human-development challenge the previous Economic & Social Progress page documents with NFHS-5 data — the two pages describe the same underlying issue from slightly different angles and time slices.
points: Education: improvement in enrolment, especially of girls, through 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao', Samagra Shiksha, Mission Prerna; Health: expansion of CHCs, PHCs, medical colleges, Ayushman Bharat, Jan Aushadhi Kendras
Skill Development: Kaushal Vikas Mission, ITIs modernisation, focus on youth employability; Digital Inclusion: BharatNet, Common Service Centres (CSCs), digital payments & DBT

Urbanization, Environment & Sustainable.intro: The Namami Gange Programme named here for Ganga rejuvenation deserves particular attention given how central the Ganga has been to this entire track — from the Vedic-age Doab settlements through Kashi's spiritual significance to the present-day environmental challenge of maintaining that same river system.
points: Rapid urbanisation with planned development; Smart City Mission projects in Lucknow, Kanpur, Varanasi, Agra, Prayagraj; Metro Rail — Lucknow, Kanpur, Agra, Noida-Greater Noida; AMRUT, Housing for All, SBM-U 2.0

Afforestation and increase in green cover; Namami Gange Programme — Ganga rejuvenation; promotion of renewable energy (Solar Policy); waste management, solid & liquid waste handling; climate change adaptation — flood control, drought management, water conservation

Major Challenges.intro: Compare this list of current challenges — regional disparity, urban congestion, farm distress — against the similar challenge list on the Economic & Social Progress page; the near-total overlap between the two pages' challenge sections is itself informative, showing these are persistent structural issues rather than one-off problems specific to a single year's data.
points: Unemployment and underemployment; regional disparities (Purvanchal, Bundelkhand); low per capita income; population pressure and urban congestion; farm distress, land fragmentation; environmental degradation and pollution; quality of education and health services; women's safety and social issues

Way Forward.intro: This category's closing framing, 'Viksit Uttar Pradesh is the foundation of Viksit Bharat', deliberately mirrors the national India 2020–Present page's own 'Viksit Bharat @2047' vision — worth reading the two pages' concluding sections together as a matched pair of regional and national aspiration.
points: Balanced regional development — Purvanchal & Bundelkhand; quality education, skill development and innovation; industrialisation with sustainability and green growth; agricultural diversification and value addition; strengthening health, nutrition and social protection
Good governance, digital transformation and citizen-centric services; inclusive growth ensuring 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas'

Expressways, Defense Corridor & 1 Trilli: Expressway State of India: UP has built India's largest high-speed expressway network: 1. Yamuna Expressway (165 km, Greater Noida to Agra), 2. Agra-Lucknow Expressway (302 km, features an airstrip for fighter jet emergency landings), 3. Purvanchal Expressway (341 km, Lucknow to Ghazipur), 4. Bundelkhand Expressway (296 km, Etawah to Chitrakoot), 5. Ganga Expressway (594 km, Meerut to Prayagraj - under construction).

Defense Industrial Corridor (UP DIC): Set up across 6 strategic nodes: Aligarh, Agra, Jhansi, Chitrakoot, Kanpur, and Lucknow; developing indigenous aerospace manufacturing, BrahMos supersonic cruise missile production unit in Lucknow, artillery shell manufacturing in Kanpur.

Aviation & Megaprojects: Jewar / Noida International Airport (poised to be India's largest international airport with 5–6 runways); Maryada Purushottam Shri Ram International Airport at Ayodhya; dedicated industrial freight corridors (EDFC and WDFC intersecting at Dadri Multi-Modal Logistics Hub).

Vision for 1 Trillion Dollar GSDP: Ambitious target to scale UP's Gross State Domestic Product to 1 trillion US dollars by 2027–2030, anchored by infrastructure investments, tourism corridors (Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, Ayodhya Dham, Braj Teerth Vikas), and green energy.

periods.tagline: From the Banks of the Ganga to the Fields of Awadh, from Ancient Sages to Modern Leaders, Uttar Pradesh Has Always Been a Land of Ideas, Courage and Contribution to India's Journey
periods.overview: This page is deliberately built to function differently from every other page in this track: rather than following a single chronological narrative, it works as a cross-cutting index of the cities and individuals — mythological, ancient, medieval, and modern — most likely to appear in UPPSC's History, Art & Culture, and Society questions, precisely because nearly every name and place listed here also has its own fuller treatment somewhere else on this site. Lord Rama's Ayodhya, Lord Krishna's Mathura, and the Buddha's Sarnath connect back to the Vedic Age, Mahajanapadas, and Maurya Period pages; Razia Sultan and Sikandar Lodi connect to the Delhi Sultanate and Sayyid-Lodi pages; Begum Hazrat Mahal, Rani Lakshmibai, and Nana Sahib connect to the Revolt of 1857 page; and Govind Ballabh Pant, Mulayam Singh Yadav, and Mayawati connect to the Political Developments page. Used this way, the page is less a standalone historical account than a deliberate doorway — exactly the function this site's knowledge graph is built to support — letting a reader start from any single name they encounter in a UPPSC question and follow it back to the fuller period, dynasty, or movement it belongs to, whether that fuller account sits within this Uttar Pradesh track or in the national chronology alongside it.

phases.name: Mythological & Vedic Figures
points: Lord Rama (Ayodhya) — ideal ruler, Maryada Purushottam, symbol of dharma; Lord Krishna (Mathura) — pivotal role in the Mahabharata, symbol of wisdom & diplomacy
Gargi Vachaknavi, Maitreyi (associated with Vedic learning centres) — Vedic scholars & philosophers who participated in debates and are known for their philosophical wisdom

phases.name: Ancient & Early Medieval Figures
points: Chanakya (Kautilya, 4th century BCE) — political thinker, author of the Arthashastra, associate of Chandragupta Maurya; Ashoka (born in Lumbini, associated with U.P., 3rd century BCE) — Mauryan emperor, propagated Buddhism, dharma & welfare
Harsha Vardhana (Kanauj, 7th century CE) — mighty ruler of Kanauj, patron of learning & Buddhism

phases.name: Medieval Figures
points: Goswami Tulsidas (16th century) — author of the Ramcharitmanas, devotee poet of Lord Rama; Raja Todar Mal (16th century) — finance minister of Akbar, land revenue reforms

Razia Sultan (13th century, associated with Badaun) — ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, known for her courage; Rani Durgavati (16th century, associated with Bundelkhand) — Gond queen who fought against Mughal forces bravely; Jahanara Begum (17th century, associated with Agra) — Mughal princess, philanthropist, builder of sarais & bazaars; Ahilyabai Holkar (18th century, associated with the Kashi corridor) — Holkar queen who built ghats in Varanasi and many temples

phases.name: 19th Century Figures
points: Begum Hazrat Mahal (Lucknow) — leader of the 1857 revolt in Awadh, symbol of courage; Nana Saheb Peshwa (Dhondu Pant) — key leader of the 1857 revolt in Kanpur; Mangal Pandey (Ballia) — freedom fighter associated with the 1857 revolt

Rani Lakshmibai (Allahabad & Jhansi) — brave warrior of the 1857 revolt, symbol of valour and sacrifice; Uda Devi Pasi (Lucknow) — brave freedom fighter of the 1857 revolt; Pt. Madan Mohan Malaviya (Prayagraj, 19th–20th century) — freedom fighter, founder of BHU, champion of education

phases.name: 20th–21st Century Figures
points: Chandra Shekhar Azad (Allahabad), Govind Ballabh Pant (Allahabad) — freedom fighter, first CM of U.P.; Dr. Sampurnanand (Varanasi); Atal Bihari Vajpayee (Gwalior-born, associated with U.P.) — former PM of India, poet, statesman

Sarojini Naidu (Prayagraj), Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit (Allahabad), Sucheta Kripalani (Lucknow) — freedom fighter, first woman CM of U.P.; Mulayam Singh Yadav (Etawah), Mayawati (Delhi, active in U.P.), Yogi Adityanath (Pauri Garhwal, associated with Gorakhpur) — political leaders of independent India's U.P.; Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam (Rameswaram, long associated with U.P. through work at DRDO) — former President of India

Important Cities of U.P..intro: Every city in this table has already appeared, in far more historical depth, on an earlier page in this track — Ayodhya on the Vedic Age page, Sarnath on the Maurya Period page, Lucknow on the Later Mughals and Revolt of 1857 pages — so treat this table as an index pointing back to those fuller accounts rather than a standalone summary.
points: Ayodhya — birthplace of Lord Ram, ancient cultural & religious centre; Varanasi — one of the world's oldest living cities, spiritual capital of India; Prayagraj (Allahabad) — confluence of Triveni, Kumbh Mela, centre of freedom struggle; Mathura — birthplace of Lord Krishna, important religious and cultural centre

Sarnath — the Buddha delivered his first sermon here, important Buddhist site; Kanpur — major industrial city, role in the freedom struggle, centre of leather & textiles; Lucknow — capital of Awadh, centre of culture, art, architecture & education; Agra — home to the Taj Mahal, major Mughal centre, tourism & industry hub; Jhansi — historical fort, symbol of resistance & valour in 1857; Meerut — birthplace of the 1857 revolt, major cantonment city

Personalities — Sports, Literature, Art.intro: This category exists specifically to cover the figures who do not fit neatly into this track's political-dynastic chronology — a novelist, a musician, a Nobel laureate — but who are just as frequently tested in UPPSC's Art & Culture and Society sections as any king or freedom fighter.
points: Sports: Major Dhyan Chand (Allahabad) — hockey wizard, Bharat Ratna; Vijay Singh (Ghazipur) — golfer; Saina Nehwal (associated with U.P.) — badminton champion

Literature: Munshi Premchand (Varanasi) — novelist, Godan, Nirmala; Harivansh Rai Bachchan (Prayagraj) — poet, Madhushala; Amritlal Nagar (Agra) — novelist, cultural chronicler; Mahadevi Verma (Farrukhabad) — poet, modern Hindi literature stalwart
Art & Music: Bismillah Khan (Dumraon, U.P.) — shehnai maestro, Bharat Ratna; Ravi Shankar (Varanasi) — sitar maestro, Bharat Ratna; Pt. Birju Maharaj (Lucknow) — Kathak exponent

Spiritual & Reformers: Swami Vivekananda (visited Kashi); Swami Ramanand (Varanasi) — Bhakti reformer; Saint Kabir (Varanasi) — Bhakti poet, social reformer; Saint Ravidas (Varanasi) — Bhakti saint, social equality
Science & Others: Dr. Har Gobind Khorana (Raipur, U.P. origin) — Nobel Laureate; Homi Bhabha (born in Mumbai, father from Allahabad) — Father of the Indian Nuclear Programme

Freedom Struggle Heroes of U.P. at a Gla.intro: This 'at a glance' table is deliberately compressed; every name here has a fuller treatment on either the Revolt of 1857 or the Freedom Struggle page earlier in this track, and this category's real purpose is simply letting you quickly check which of those two pages a given name belongs to.
points: Leaders of the 1857 Revolt: Nana Saheb, Rani Lakshmibai, Begum Hazrat Mahal, Kunwar Singh (Bihar, associated with U.P. areas), Mangal Pandey
Revolutionaries: Chandra Shekhar Azad, Ram Prasad Bismil (Shahjahanpur), Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh, Sachindra Nath Sanyal

Kisan Leaders: Baba Ramchandra (Awadh Kisan Movement), Swami Sahajanand Saraswati (Kisan leader); Gandhian Leaders: Govind Ballabh Pant, Purushottam Das Tandon, Jawaharlal Nehru (associated with Allahabad), Brahm Dutt Dwivedi

Luminaries of Uttar Pradesh: Spiritual & Literary Giants: Sage Valmiki (Bithoor on Ganga); Ved Vyasa; Goswami Tulsidas (Rajapur / Varanasi - Ramcharitmanas, Vinaya Patrika); Sant Kabir (Varanasi - Bijak; Maghar nirvana); Surdas (Runkata, Agra - Sursagar); Amir Khusrau (Patiyali, Kasganj - inventor of Sitar, Qawwali, Hindavi poet); Malik Muhammad Jayasi (Jais, Amethi - Padmavat); Bharatendu Harishchandra (Varanasi - "Father of Modern Hindi Literature"); Munshi Premchand (Lamhi, Varanasi - Godan, Gaban, Idgah); Suryakant Tripathi Nirala; Jaishankar Prasad; Mahadevi Verma; Harivansh Rai Bachchan.

Mughal Courtiers & Artists: Raja Todar Mal (Laharpur, Sitapur - creator of Dahsala revenue system); Raja Birbal (Mahesh Das, Kalpi - Navaratna court wit); Ustad Bismillah Khan (Varanasi - Shehnai maestro, Bharat Ratna 2001); Pandit Ravi Shankar (Varanasi - Sitar maestro, Bharat Ratna 1999); Begum Akhtar (Faizabad - Queen of Ghazals).

Patriots & Statesmen: Mangal Pandey (Ballia); Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi); Begum Hazrat Mahal (Lucknow); Chandra Shekhar Azad (Unnao/Allahabad); Ram Prasad Bismil (Shahjahanpur); Ashfaqulla Khan (Shahjahanpur); Motilal Nehru & Jawaharlal Nehru (Allahabad); Madan Mohan Malaviya (Prayagraj); Purushottam Das Tandon; Rafi Ahmad Kidwai; Chaudhary Charan Singh (Meerut/Baghpat - Champion of Indian Kisans); Atal Bihari Vajpayee (Bateshwar, Agra / Lucknow).

prelims: Amir Khusrau was born in Patiyali (Kasganj district, UP) in 1253 CE, and was celebrated as the "Tuti-i-Hind" (Parrot of India).
Munshi Premchand, the greatest novelist of modern Hindi and Urdu literature (author of Godan and Gaban), was born in Lamhi village near Varanasi.
Raja Todar Mal, the architect of Akbar's Dahsala land revenue system, hailed from Laharpur in Sitapur district of Uttar Pradesh.
Raja Birbal (original name Mahesh Das), one of Akbar's Nine Gems, was born in Kalpi in Jalaun district of Uttar Pradesh.
Shehnai virtuoso Ustad Bismillah Khan, who performed on the ramparts of Red Fort on India's Independence Day in 1947, was based in Varanasi and awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001.
Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, and Roshan Singh, legendary martyrs of the Kakori Action (1925), all hailed from Shahjahanpur district, UP.
Mahadevi Verma, the celebrated Hindi Chhayavadi poetess and Jnanpith laureate, was born in Farrukhabad, Uttar Pradesh.
mains: Examine the literary and cultural contributions of Uttar Pradesh to the development of Hindi and Urdu literature, highlighting Munshi Premchand, Bharatendu Harishchandra, and Amir Khusrau.
Analyze the revolutionary sacrifices of Shahjahanpur martyrs (Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan) and Chandra Shekhar Azad in India's freedom struggle.
Discuss the contributions of Chaudhary Charan Singh to peasant mobilization, agrarian reforms, and democratic politics in Northern India.

prelimsFacts: Bara Imambara & Bhool Bhulaiya (1784, Lucknow): Architectural masterpiece commissioned by Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula as a royal food-for-work famine relief project; features a colossal 50-meter unsupported central vaulted hall built without timber or iron columns, enveloped by the world-famous Bhool Bhulaiya (labyrinthine maze of 489 identical interlocking arched doorways) and flanked by the monumental Rumi Darwaza.

Sharqi Architectural Propylon Screens of Jaunpur: The Atala Masjid (1408 CE) and Lal Darwaza Masjid constructed by the Sharqi rulers of Jaunpur featured massive sloping propylon archways concealing the rear domes, symbolizing Jaunpur's status as 'Shiraz of the East' (Shiraz-i-Hind).

Kalinjar Fort & Death of Sher Shah Suri (1545 CE, Banda district): Historic Bundelkhand stronghold where Sher Shah Suri suffered fatal burns from an exploding artillery rocket (Ukka) during a military siege.
